item.title: AI agents now control part of Deepmind's compute for Gemini experiments, but recursive self-improvement remains distant
item.description:
【the-decoder.com】Google Deepmind uses AI agents to run experiments on their own for upcoming Gemini models. Research chief Koray Kavukcuoglu says the lab is still far from recursive self-improvement. For oversight, Deepmind intentionally leaves the agents' internal chains of thought untrained so they can be reviewed. Kavukcuoglu measures AGI by everyday user trust rather than benchmarks. The article AI agents now control part of Deepmind's compute for Gemini experiments, but recursive self-improvement remains distant appeared first on The Decoder.

item.title: Anthropic study shows the hardest part of adopting AI at work has little to do with learning the tools
item.description:
【the-decoder.com】Anthropic studied nearly 300 AI deployments across 58 US companies with sobering results. Nearly one in five still delivers no business value, held back by heavy review workloads, internal bottlenecks, and employee resistance. The researchers say the biggest hurdles stem from outdated company structures. The article Anthropic study shows the hardest part of adopting AI at work has little to do with learning the tools appeared first on The Decoder.

item.title: MIT team discovers that unrealistic training data makes AI climate predictions more reliable
item.description:
【the-decoder.com】MIT researchers have developed a method that lets AI climate models get by with a single training run instead of the usual six to eight. An algorithm generates deliberately unrealistic scenarios with extreme CO2 or methane swings that make the model more robust. Until now, these emulators were often outdated by the time they were finished, according to the researchers.
